knowledge.text: The actual edit adds a conditional amount-role distinction to otherwise general label-matching guidance. On the amount question, Parent states a subtotal-to-total substitution and scores hard=0, ANLS=0.6; Candidate submits the reference-matching answer and scores hard=1, ANLS=1. This supports testing amount-role guidance where the question distinguishes roles, but does not show what the image contains, what Candidate attended to, or that the edit caused the gain. In the other supplied pair, a previously correct invoice-date answer changes its year and regresses from hard=1, ANLS=1 to hard=0, ANLS=10/11. That question has no explicit amount-role trigger; the available text does not explain the regression or tie it to this clause. Across both pairs, one observed gain is offset by one observed loss, so this batch does not establish a general improvement or harmlessness. Both the positive observation and the regression remain relevant despite causal uncertainty. For the amount pair, whether a matching label existed is unknown. Candidate silence about labels cannot establish absence or visual adherence; the pair cannot be excluded from consideration on that basis.
